rated_messages.input_message: Urges are like annoying ads. You might see them but you don't have to buy what they're selling.
See what it is like to let the urge pass. You can have an urge and choose not to smoke.
Instead of smoking, take 10 deep, slow breaths and count them. Pay attention to what your breathing feels like. If you lose count, that's okay, just start over at 1 until you get to 10.
Some places trigger powerful cravings, that is to be expected. Stop and notice where in your body you feel those cravings and remind yourself that cravings typically pass in 1 to 3 minutes
Feelings aren't permanent. They are always changing like the weather. Observe the storm that is coming, but don't fight it. Eventually the weather will change.
Ask yourself, "What do I need right now? Is it really a smoke, or is there something else I need? How can I best take care of myself right now?"

Remind yourself that by staying quit, you'll be freeing yourself from the constant cycle of cigarette, nicotine withdrawal, feeling stressed as a result and wanting another cigarette. Keep going and this will be a thing of the past!

Imagine walking into a social situation in three months' time as a non-smoker. Now hold that picture and imagine you're that person now. Seeing yourself as a non-smoker now can make it much easier to resist!
Picture the people or things you care deeply about. On a scale of 0-10, how willing are you to let this urge pass for those reasons?
